title: TCS formalizations: sunflowers, the metric TSP integrality gap, and quantum query complexity
description:
Machine-checked Lean 4 formalizations (over Mathlib) of the improved sunflower bounds — Alweiss–Lovett–Wu–Zhang (STOC 2020), Rao's Coding for Sunflowers, and the Bell–Chueluecha–Warnke (C·r·log w)^w improvement — through the ALWZ and Rao–BCW approaches, together with lower bounds for robust-sunflower thresholds, the BCW satisfying/spread condition, and the classical Erdős–Rado theorem.

The Lean sources are sorry-free; a checks file included in the default build verifies with #guard_msgs that the flagship theorems depend on exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The accompanying formalization notes record boundary cases, implicit constructions, and proof-engineering choices that required explicit treatment, including the reconstruction of Rao's case-1 decoder and the base-1.9 treatment of the w = 2 logarithm boundary.

The TSP development follows Karlin–Klein–Oveis Gharan, Gurvits–Klein–Leake and Song and proves a metric subtour-LP integrality-gap bound of 3/2 - 2.05522 × 10-30. It includes 668 Song regression examples and an enforced axiom inventory. The formalized TSP claim is tour existence; polynomial running time and finite-precision sampling are outside its scope. Proof notes describe the adaptations of the printed arguments.

The quantum query library formalizes the negative-weight adversary bound, its duality and composition theory, and its characterization of bounded-error query complexity for total Boolean functions. It also includes a finite quantum query model, oracle simulations, the polynomial method, amplitude amplification and estimation, robust search, quantum-walk search, and explicit query bounds for classic examples. Regression tests and direct axiom audits accompany the library; its guide records the precise oracle conventions and theorem scope.
